analysis:
Documentation-only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md. Three edits: a date bump (line 3), a note that GLM video input also accepts variable-frame-rate inline mp4/quicktime (head line 52), and a new file-path table row for ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json (DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE, mode 0600). The row records that managed GLM load hashes are bound to file identities and reused for startup registration. The new row is in the patch excerpt near head line 1578; the head text supplied covers only lines 1-404, so that region was not visible. No code, config or default changes are in the supplied evidence.

Threat-model relevance: the verified-weights store touches A-004 and T-012/T-027 (weight substitution and weight-hash verification). Reusing a cached hash at registration is only safe if the binding to file identity (size, mtime, inode and similar) is robust against an operator swapping weights. The operator controls the weights directory and could in principle preserve metadata while altering content. The documentation says the binding exists, but the implementation, VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift, is not supplied, so nothing can be concluded. The base text also describes the hash-reuse and rehash behavior for model switch: 'metadata changes and mandatory fresh/SSD checks still rehash'. This is an existing trust assumption, not a regression shown here.

The VFR video note is runtime behavior in the media decode path (T-050 covers inline video temp files). The implementing change is not supplied, so its security effects (decoder attack surface, temp-file handling) need review in the code PR. No new attack surface, authorization or encryption change is visible in these docs.

Integration questions for a deeper pass: how VerifiedWeightHashStore binds hashes to file identity, whether the 0600 file is protected from operator tampering (it is not, under ADV-001, so the coordinator's own verification must remain authoritative), and how VFR video decoding handles untrusted consumer-supplied media.
